question: Determine whether the system $x+y+z=3$, $2x-y+z=0$ and $x+2y-z=3$ is consistent by examining the determinant of its coefficient matrix.
explanation:
Step 1: Form the coefficient matrix
The coefficient matrix is $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1\\2&-1&1\\1&2&-1\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 2: Evaluate its determinant
Expanding along the first row, $$|A|=1\begin{vmatrix}-1&1\\2&-1\end{vmatrix}-1\begin{vmatrix}2&1\\1&-1\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}2&-1\\1&2\end{vmatrix}$$
Step 3: Simplify
Thus, $$|A|=(-1)-(-3)+5=7$$
Step 4: Interpret the result
Since $|A|=7\ne0$, the coefficient matrix is nonsingular. Therefore, the system has a unique solution.
Hence, the given system is consistent.

options.B: The system is consistent with infinitely many solutions because $|A|=0$.
options.C: The system is consistent with a unique solution because $|A|=7\ne0$.
